id.description: Intervention-request id: "ir-<yyyymmddThhmmss>-<4hex>" (UTC timestamp + 4 lowercase hex), e.g. "ir-20260929T101500-beef".

runId.description: Run id: "<kind>-<yyyymmddThhmmss>-<4hex>" with kind discovery|replay and a UTC timestamp, e.g. "replay-20260929T101500-a1b2". Names the run evidence directory.

runKind.description: What produced a run: an LLM-driven discovery run or a deterministic replay run.

kind.description: approval: an irreversible action awaits an operator decision. takeover: the run is stuck and asks an operator to drive the same live session.

text.description: Human-readable explanation. Redacted before the request is built.

id.description: Capability id: a lowercase kebab-case slug, e.g. "member-lookup". Stable across artifact versions.

version.description: Version of the capability being replayed.

oneOf.description: A replay run: the capability being executed.

goal.description: The natural-language discovery goal, with sensitive values as {{param}} placeholders. Redacted before the request is built.

oneOf.description: A discovery run: the goal the agent is pursuing.

subject.description: What the run is doing: a capability (replay) or a goal (discovery).

index.description: 0-based step index (replay) or action count so far (discovery).

id.description: The artifact step id; absent in discovery, which has no steps yet.

description.description: What the paused step does, e.g. "Click Confirm". Redacted before the request is built.

risk.description: Risk class of an action: read (observes only), reversible (changes state that can be undone, e.g. typing into a field), irreversible (commits a business change, e.g. Confirm). Policy gates on it; replay recomputes it and never lowers it.

currentStep.description: The step or action the run paused before.

url.description: The current page URL. Redacted before the request is built.

screenshotRef.description: Masked screenshot at pause time; null if capture failed.

a11ySnapshotRef.description: Redacted accessibility snapshot at pause time; null if capture failed.

state.description: What the screen looked like when the run paused.

items.description: How a request was resolved. approve/reject: an approval request was answered. resumed: the operator took control and handed it back. aborted: the operator ended the run.

options.description: The decisions the operator may take, without duplicates.

status.description: open: waiting. claimed: an operator took it (and may hold control). resolved: decided.

resolution.description: The decision; present exactly when status is resolved.

decision.description: How a request was resolved. approve/reject: an approval request was answered. resumed: the operator took control and handed it back. aborted: the operator ended the run.

createdAt.description: When the request was raised (ISO 8601, UTC).

description: A request for a human: approve an irreversible action or take over the same live session. Built from redacted data only; screenshots are masked (invariant 3).

id.description: Evidence id: a lowercase kebab-case slug unique within the run, e.g. "screenshot-0003".

kind.description: What the evidence file holds: a masked screenshot, a redacted accessibility snapshot, a Playwright trace (local only), a redacted JSON document, or a redacted log.

path.description: A POSIX path relative to the run directory, e.g. "screenshots/0003-s06-click-search.png". No leading "/", no "." or ".." segment, no backslash, no scheme: evidence can never point outside its run.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the stored file bytes, as 64 lowercase hex characters. Detects tampering.

redacted.description: Always true: the file passed the redaction layer (or screenshot masking) before it was stored. A literal, so an unredacted ref cannot be represented (invariant 3).

localOnly.description: true for files that stay on the machine that produced them (e.g. traces, which cannot be fully masked); they are never copied into shared evidence.

EvidenceRef.description: A pointer to one stored evidence file of a run. The contract carries refs, never the evidence content.
